newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary, McDonnell Douglas sign agreement.
newsitem.headline: Hungary, McDonnell Douglas sign agreement.

text.p: Hungary and McDonnell Douglas of the U.S., which wants to sell fighter jets to Hungary, concluded an industrial cooperation agreement on Thursday, the government said in a statement.

Sweden's SAAB AB, another candidate for selling fighters to Hungary, was the first company, with which an agreement was signed to help Hungary pay for potential aircraft shipments in the framework of industrial cooperation projects.
"We also agreed with McDonnell Douglas -- under the same conditions as with SAAB - about the rules of industrial cooperation and covering the price," the statement said. @
Government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference on Thursday that part of the cooperation programme will be carried out even if Hungary decides not to buy the aircraft.
McDonnell Douglas has begun negotiations with 75 Hungarian companies, the Hungarian MTI news agency said on Thursday.
The government did not disclose financial details.

However, the statement said that only transactions improving Hungary's current account could be used for financing the aircraft shipments, for example export deals, investments and supplies from Hungarian companies. @

McDonnell Douglas, maker of the F-18 Hornet, is competing for post-Cold War business in central Europe against SAAB, which makes the "Gripen," Lockheed Martin's F-16s, France's "Mirage" and other European builders.
Defence ministry sources said earlier this year that Hungary -- depending on the timescale of its hoped-for NATO membership -- is looking to buy some 30 fighters.
